A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete text, equations, ten figures and appendix analyses support reliable comparison despite reformatting and section moves.

before.justification: v1 reports original correlation and resampling analyses of existing MLLM evaluation records, including MathVista filtering experiments and appendix redundancy maps.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses in Section 3 and Appendix B, including instance redundancy results and cross-benchmark comparisons.

M1.justification: The performance-correlation framework, dimension and benchmark averaging, instance subsampling, and Top-K analysis remain unchanged. Section 2 contains wording refinements without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both retain the MMBench dimension study, 18-benchmark instance analysis, four mathematical benchmarks, and AI2D and SEED-Bench appendix analyses. The MathVista filtering scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing redundancy-estimation methods against the framework. No comparison method is added or removed from the retained analyses.

E3.justification: Both specify MMBench v1.1, the same Top-50/Bottom-50 selection rule, 37 models for the mathematical-benchmark analysis, and the 0.95 similarity threshold. Metrics, subsampling and MathVista filtering procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The model-tier comparisons, benchmark-specific redundancy curves, and removal of general-VQA and CLEVR-derived MathVista questions are retained. Appendix B preserves the earlier AI2D and SEED-Bench analyses.

E5.justification: Both specify 100 sampling iterations and report average correlations. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The corresponding plotted data and reported findings are unchanged, including appendix heatmaps. For example, Figure 8 retains MathVision–MathVista SRCC of 0.84 before filtering and 0.90 after removing general-VQA and CLEVR-derived questions.

T1.justification: Section 2's assumption and Equations 1-4 are retained, as are the metric formulas moved from appendix Section 6 to Appendix A. The new limitations provide qualitative qualifications without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three levels of redundancy, empirical scope and benchmark-design contributions. Wording changes do not redefine the central claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explains that similar capabilities may yield divergent rankings and that correlation metrics may miss task difficulty, behavioral differences and outlier effects. It also makes the previously discussed dependence on model selection an explicit limitation.

D1.justification: The same VLMEvalKit/OpenVLMRecords and OpenCompass Reasoning Leaderboard data-access disclosures are retained. No implementation details, processing instructions or reproducibility settings are added.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Conversion from numbered citations to author-year citations and bibliography reordering do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v2 lightly shortens introduction and framework prose and corrects Section 3.1's figure-description wording. Practice recommendations move from Section 4 to Appendix C, and limitations and acknowledgements sections are added; the remaining narrative closely matches v1.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes page geometry from Letter to A4, typography, margins, caption styling and figure placement. Figure 4 is separated from Figure 3 onto another page, and Figures 3, 9 and 10 adopt 50+/50- panel labels. All ten figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: New Section 5 makes specific weaknesses of the central correlation assumption and redundancy metrics explicit, improving interpretive transparency. The empirical evidence and practical recommendations are preserved. This is a limited improvement in explaining applicability, without additional validation or correction of those weaknesses.
